# The case the ecosystem markers exist for: a dependency the person compiling
# cannot edit. The package ships types in a .d.ts and code in a .js, and only
# the .d.ts carries the annotation — which is the only file the importer reads.
#
# The bare specifier goes to node unchanged, so node's own node_modules lookup
# is what finds the runnable file. A *relative* import is resolved by the same
# resolver the checker uses, and that one answers with types — so `./vendor`
# below lands on a .d.ts, which describes a module without being one, and the
# evaluator has to run the .js beside it instead.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

grep 'SLUG-FROM-A-DEPENDENCY' out/index.html
grep 'vendored-answer' out/index.html
! grep 'toUpperCase' out/index.html
! grep 'toLowerCase' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"
import slug "js:slugify"
import vendor "js:./vendor"

const s = slug.slugify("slug from a dependency")
const v = vendor.answer()

component main {
    text(value=s)
    text(value=v)
}
-- node_modules/slugify/package.json --
{
  "name": "slugify",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "index.js",
  "types": "index.d.ts"
}
-- node_modules/slugify/index.d.ts --
/** @__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__ */
export declare function slugify(s: string): string;
-- node_modules/slugify/index.js --
export function slugify(s) {
    return s.toUpperCase().split(" ").join("-");
}
-- vendor/index.d.ts --
/** @sngl-pure */
export declare function answer(): string;
-- vendor/index.js --
export function answer() {
    return "VENDORED-ANSWER".toLowerCase();
}
